set.body:
Why (highest leverage): PairedDualityDiagram holds two diagrams plus a shared sample space, but the paired estimators mostly ignore it and compute unweighted cross-products: PLSC uses X transpose Y, CCA forms separate unweighted covariance/cross-covariance matrices, and RRR builds a bespoke fitted-response SVD path. Two-table methods should be the SVD of the shared-row-metric cross-operator Q_X^(1/2) X transpose D Y Q_Y^(1/2): PLSC=(I,I); CCA=(Sxx^-1,Syy^-1) with ridge expressed through the metric; RRR=asymmetric, with direction determining the metric choice.

Scope: add DualityKernels.crossGram(paired, policy) computing the metric-weighted cross-operator with the same storage discipline as rowGram/colGram; re-express Plsc/Cca/ReducedRankRegression as one PairedGmd routine parameterized by (Q_X,Q_Y). Regularization becomes a metric and direction becomes a metric choice. The win is cohesion, free D-weighting, and deleting three bespoke numeric paths; it is not a speed claim, because CCA still forms and inverts the column Gram.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] crossGram added with storage-policy handling and tests (dense, diagonal-metric, sparse) mirroring DualityKernelsSuite.
- [ ] Plsc/Cca/RRR share one PairedGmd routine; the three bespoke cross-product paths are deleted.
- [ ] A non-identity row metric D produces D-weighted PLSC/CCA, covered by a test.
- [ ] Ridge regularization is expressed as a Q metric, not a code branch.
- [ ] Paired parity fixtures pass unchanged for the identity-D case on JVM+JS.

Blocked by the parity-fixtures item, the unified-LatentFit/Spectrum item, and the projection-contract MvMap item.
